model: Series AVPT pencil-style air velocity transmitter, BACnet MS/TP
aliases: AVPT pencil style air velocity transmitter
applies_to: Dwyer Series AVPT thermal-anemometer duct velocity transmitters ordered with the BACnet MS/TP output.
summary: The AVPT is a pencil-style thermal anemometer probe for duct air velocity, sold with either analog outputs or a BACnet MS/TP output. On BACnet it exposes velocity and air temperature as four Analog Inputs (each in imperial and metric), plus objects to set the MS/TP address, the baud rate and a factory reset.
notes: Velocity and temperature are each given twice, in imperial and metric units, as separate objects.
The overview table prints BV 1 as "Restore Factory Defauls"; the property table spells it "Restore Factory Defaults".
Factory address is 127; the device instance follows the address until a specific instance is written.

source.title: Series AVPT Pencil Style Air Velocity Transmitter - Specifications, Installation and Operating Instructions

integration.summary: Set a unique MS/TP address (PIV 1, then power cycle), let auto-baud lock onto the bus, and read velocity and temperature in the units you need (AI 1-4).
setup: Ships at MS/TP address 127; write the new address to PIV 1 and reset or power cycle the device.
Auto-baud is on by default (9600 to 115200, 8N1); it locks in after the first Who-Is or ReadProperty it answers.
Device instance defaults to 607xxx (xxx = address) until a specific instance is written.
DeviceCommunicationControl and ReinitializeDevice need the password "Dwyer".
Max Master changes need a power cycle.
gotchas: The device may not answer while auto-baud is still detecting the bus speed.
Default comms settings can also be restored by wiring: briefly connect the white CFG wire to ground as the manual describes.
